target_customer: Finance teams at startups and mid market companies (examples named on the site: Zapier, Turo, Harvey, Chess.com)
problem: Finance teams export data from many systems into spreadsheets for budgeting, reporting and forecasting; Aleph syncs spreadsheet models with live data.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, spreadsheet add-ins plus web app
product_category: FP&A and financial data management software

founders.name: Albert Gozzi
prior_employers: a startup (as CFO, name not given)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he built the first version himself in 2020.

founders.name: Santiago Perez De Rosso
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he joined in 2021 before YC. Education and employers not found in a source opened. Technical flag from his CTO role.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs many reliable integrations, spreadsheet add-ins that sync live data and a modeling layer; standard but broad engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Once finance models and data pipelines live in the tool, switching is costly, but spreadsheet based rivals such as Cube and DataRails existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying Aleph. Rival Mosaic was later bought by HiBob per an unrelated search result.

market_need_then: Finance teams were doing budgeting and forecasting in disconnected spreadsheets. TechCrunch frames Aleph as reconciling disparate financial data; no dated spend figures for 2021 were found.

branding.domain_note: Operates on getaleph.com (get prefix) because the plain name is used by others.
branding.community_and_virality: G2 badges and a 4.9 rating are claimed on the site; the name is shared with Aleph Farms, Aleph Alpha and others which dilutes search

brand_strength.rationale: Name collides with several better known brands, and no press about the brand itself was found; the product does get trade coverage.

outcome_analysis: Aleph came out of stealth in October 2023 with 16.7M USD from Bain Capital Ventures, Khosla, Picus and YC, and raised a 29M USD Series B in September 2025 for total funding near 46M USD. The company says it grew ten times after the first round and wins customers like Zapier and Turo. Spreadsheet first positioning and fast implementation fit the demand, though crowded FP&A competition remains.
notes: The 2023 round is recorded as stage other because press describes 16.7M USD in funding led by Bain Capital Ventures including a Series A, and the Series B post lists a seed (Khosla led) and a Series A (Bain led) without separate amounts; the 16.7M may combine seed and Series A. Total raised is 46M USD per the company; one aggregator says 5.2M and one UK outlet says the Series B was 21.3M GBP. Competitors are cited from a 2023 TechCrunch article (later than the 2021 batch), which names Anaplan and Adaptive as incumbents and Mosaic, Pigment, OnPlan, Casual, Cube and DataRails as newer tools; only the incumbents are listed because the others have no dated source near 2021. Founders education not found. Outcome search returned only other companies named Aleph.
